change.author: Carina Wollendorfer

findings.title: Team admin check requires admin AND owner
findings.body: `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` is true only for someone who is both. Team admins who are not owners are denied, and `teamId ?? 0` queries a nonexistent team for non-team bookings. This is most likely meant to be `||`, or to use a membership check that accepts either role. Also, `isAttendee` lets any attendee add arbitrary guests; confirm that is intended.

findings.title: Dedup and blacklist are case-sensitive and not applied to the email list
findings.body: The blacklist is lowercased, but `guest` is compared as-is, so `Foo@X.com` bypasses the blacklist. The comparison with existing attendees is also case-sensitive. Duplicate entries within `guests` are only checked client-side, so a direct API call can create duplicate attendees. Separately, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` at line 168 receives the raw `guests` rather than `uniqueGuests`. Skipped guests that are already attendees therefore get the 'new booking' email, and the match is case-sensitive. Lowercase and dedupe the input, and pass `uniqueGuests` to the email function.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the organizer's
findings.body: When an attendee or team admin adds guests, the EventManager is built from `ctx.user`'s credentials. The booking's references belong to the organizer's calendar, so the update will probably not reach the organizer's calendar event. `booking.user.credentials` is already loaded in the query and is unused. Consider using the organizer's credentials. Also, `updateCalendarAttendees` only logs an error when references are empty, and the handler still reports success.

findings.title: Email failure is swallowed without logging the error
findings.body: The catch logs a fixed string and drops `err`, so failures cannot be diagnosed. Log the error object.

findings.title: Error toast fallback is unreachable and prefixes the raw code
findings.body: The template string is always truthy, so `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` never runs. The toast also shows an internal code, e.g. 'FORBIDDEN: ...'. Zod validation errors from the server are also passed to `t()` as raw JSON. Use `err.message ? t(err.message) : t("unable_to_add_guests")`.

findings.title: Empty entries and stale error state
findings.body: The initial value is `[""]`, and submitting with an empty field fails validation with a generic message. `isInvalidEmail` is never cleared on edit or after a successful add. After success, the error flag can still be set the next time the dialog opens.

findings.title: Action id and label are mismatched
findings.body: The id `add_members` and the label `additional_guests` do not match the feature ('add guests'). Because the action is in `editBookingActions`, it also shows for bookings where it cannot work, such as ones without calendar references.

contracts.before_after: Adds attendees to the DB, updates the calendar through EventManager, sends emails, and the UI invalidates the bookings list.
contracts.visible_effect: A toast appears and the bookings list refreshes.
contracts.failure_mode: Email errors are swallowed. A wrong permission check denies team admins. The calendar update uses the caller's credentials.
contracts.open_question: Is the editLocation handler's permission check the intended model?

summary: The add-guests feature has a likely wrong permission check (`isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner`). Its dedup and blacklist logic is case-sensitive and the emails use the unfiltered `guests` list. The calendar update uses the caller's credentials rather than the organizer's. The dialog's error toast fallback is also unreachable. Per the Environment note I did not read `editLocation.handler.ts`, so the comparison against the existing location-edit path is incomplete and the contract is left open.
